status.headline: Eisenkot targets a government as early as Dec 2; Together not yet signed; Democrats deal agreed in principle, not reported signed
status.summary: Gadi Eisenkot's mandate runs to December 6 (extendable by up to 14 days), and the Jerusalem Post reports the goal is to swear in a government as early as Wednesday, December 2. Yisrael Beiteinu agreed on November 24 to sign a coalition deal, and the Democrats agreed on terms on November 26; Eisenkot described both as signed agreements, but the Jerusalem Post and Jewish Chronicle describe the Democrats deal as agreed in principle ahead of signing, so the site lists neither as formally signed. Bennett's Together has not signed; his meeting with Eisenkot was moved to Sunday at Bennett's request, pending a detailed conscription framework. Unity talks with Likud continue, with each side blaming the other for the pace, and UTJ talks centre on the draft and on ending arrests of yeshiva students.
watch: Will the Yashar–Democrats and Yashar–Yisrael Beiteinu agreements be confirmed as formally signed?
Will the Sunday Eisenkot–Bennett meeting produce a deal with Together?
Will UTJ's rabbinic leadership approve a draft-law framework, and will UTJ back or abstain on an Eisenkot government?
Will a government be presented to the Knesset by about December 2, or will Eisenkot seek an extension?

parties.name: Joint List

leader.name: Yousef Jabareen
leader.bio: Legal scholar and former Hadash MK who now heads the Joint List.

parties.about: Alliance of Arab and Arab-Jewish parties: Hadash, Ta'al and Balad.
parties.stance: Recommended Eisenkot on Nov 5, putting him at 67. Says it will support him from outside the government, not join it.

parties.name: Ra'am

leader.name: Mansour Abbas
leader.bio: Led Ra'am into the 2021 Bennett–Lapid government, the first time an Arab party joined an Israeli coalition.

parties.about: Islamist-conservative party rooted in the southern branch of the Islamic Movement.
parties.stance: Recommended Eisenkot. Says it will vote for an Eisenkot government even without a formal coalition agreement.

parties.name: The Democrats

leader.name: Yair Golan
leader.bio: Former IDF deputy chief of staff. Took over Labor in 2024 and led its merger with Meretz into The Democrats.

parties.about: Left-wing party formed by the merger of Labor and Meretz.
parties.stance: Recommended Eisenkot. Reached understandings with Yashar on Nov 26 to sign a coalition deal; reported terms give it Public Security, Labor and Welfare, Communications, and Culture and Sport.

parties.name: Together (Beyachad)

leader.name: Naftali Bennett
leader.bio: Prime minister 2021–22 and former leader of Yamina. Runs Together jointly with Yair Lapid, founder of Yesh Atid and prime minister in the second half of 2022.

parties.about: Joint list of Bennett's party and Yair Lapid's Yesh Atid.
parties.stance: Recommended Eisenkot. Bennett backs a unity government with Eisenkot as first prime minister; he has not signed a deal, and his meeting with Eisenkot was moved to Sunday pending a detailed conscription framework. Lapid's camp differs over whether Netanyahu can be in it. Bennett denies a Haaretz report of a back channel to Netanyahu's camp.

parties.name: Yashar

leader.name: Gadi Eisenkot
leader.bio: IDF chief of staff 2015–19. Joined Benny Gantz's National Unity in 2022 and sat in the wartime cabinet, then left to found Yashar.

parties.about: New centrist party, now the second-largest in the Knesset.
parties.stance: Holds the mandate. Pursuing several tracks at once: unity talks with Likud, a haredi deal on the draft, and Arab outside support. Agreed with Yisrael Beiteinu on Nov 24 to sign a coalition deal and reached terms with the Democrats on Nov 26; says it aims to sign with Together soon.

parties.name: Yisrael Beiteinu

leader.name: Avigdor Liberman
leader.bio: Founded Yisrael Beiteinu in 1999. Former defence minister and finance minister, and a long-time advocate of drafting haredi men.

parties.about: Secular right-wing party with roots among immigrants from the former Soviet Union.
parties.stance: First party to agree to sign a coalition deal with Yashar (Nov 24); reported preliminary terms give it Defense, Justice and Aliyah and Integration. Would accept a government backed by UTJ and possibly Ra'am, provided it has a Jewish majority; opposes the talks with Likud.

parties.name: Likud

leader.name: Benjamin Netanyahu
leader.bio: Israel's longest-serving prime minister (1996–99, 2009–21, and since December 2022). On trial in three corruption cases, which he denies.

parties.about: Largest party in the Knesset and the core of every right-wing government since 2009.
parties.stance: Calls for a 'national unity' government without Arab parties. Talks with Yashar continue; the Jerusalem Post reports an agreement in principle on advancing judicial changes by consensus, with Ben-Gvir's place in a government unresolved. Eisenkot accuses Likud of stalling; Likud says its hand is extended.

parties.name: Shas

leader.name: Aryeh Deri
leader.bio: Has led the Sephardi ultra-Orthodox party for most of the time since the late 1980s. Former interior minister.

parties.about: Sephardi and Mizrahi ultra-Orthodox party, a fixture of Netanyahu governments.
parties.stance: Recommended Netanyahu. Deri has not decided whether to cross over and is reported to be abroad and not part of the talks; a reported plan would bring Shas in at a later stage.

parties.name: United Torah Judaism

leader.name: Ya'akov Asher
leader.bio: Chairs United Torah Judaism's Knesset faction in the 26th Knesset.

parties.about: Ashkenazi ultra-Orthodox alliance of Agudat Yisrael and Degel HaTorah.
parties.stance: Declined to recommend anyone. In talks with Eisenkot and Liberman, led by Yaakov Asher; Liberman says its rabbis approved negotiating. Wants arrests of yeshiva students ended before a swearing-in, which Eisenkot is reported unwilling to make a precondition. A single outlet reported on Nov 26 draft-law understandings pending sign-off by Rabbi Hirsch; UTJ denies negotiating cabinet posts.

parties.name: Religious Zionism–Zehut

leader.name: Bezalel Smotrich
leader.bio: Finance minister in the outgoing government, also responsible for civil affairs in the West Bank.

parties.about: Pro-settlement religious-nationalist list, running with Zehut.
parties.stance: Recommended Netanyahu. Eisenkot has signalled he may also hold talks with it.

parties.name: Otzma Yehudit

leader.name: Itamar Ben-Gvir
leader.bio: National security minister in the outgoing government. A lawyer and long-time far-right activist.

parties.stance: Recommended Netanyahu. Opposed to any government that relies on Arab parties.

scenarios.name: National unity
scenarios.note: One seat short on these three alone. Stuck on who leads and on a rotation deal; Bennett won't sit under Netanyahu, Lapid is wary of Netanyahu at all.

scenarios.name: Change bloc + Arab outside support
scenarios.note: The 67 who recommended Eisenkot. Arab parties would support from outside; Liberman has resisted relying on them.

scenarios.name: Change bloc + haredi parties
scenarios.note: Exactly 61. Needs a deal on the draft that both Liberman and the haredim can live with; the Democrats would likely balk.

scenarios.name: Change bloc + UTJ
scenarios.note: A minority government. Could pass a confidence vote only if Ra'am and others abstain or vote yes, since it needs more yes than no votes.

timeline.title: Jerusalem Post: aim is to swear in a government as early as December 2
timeline.text: A Jerusalem Post analysis says the goal is a swearing-in as early as Wednesday, December 2, with a confidence vote soon after the president is notified. It reports that Yashar and Likud teams reached an agreement in principle on advancing judicial changes by consensus, while Yashar opposes Ben-Gvir in government and Netanyahu has not agreed to drop him. UTJ wants arrests of yeshiva students halted before swearing-in, which Eisenkot is reported unwilling to make a precondition. The paper describes the Democrats deal as agreed in principle ahead of signing and says Bennett has not signed.

timeline.title: Eisenkot says he will form a government within his mandate; Bennett meeting moved to Sunday
timeline.text: Eisenkot said on November 27 that he would form a government within the eight days left in his mandate, and that he was working to sign with Bennett's Together soon. He called the week's progress the signing of agreements with Yisrael Beiteinu and the Democrats, though the Jewish Chronicle describes the Democrats deal as agreed on terms. Walla, as relayed by the Times of Israel, reported that Bennett postponed their meeting to Sunday because no detailed conscription framework had been presented. Eisenkot accused Likud of stalling unity talks, and Likud said its hand remained extended.

timeline.title: Report: Yashar and UTJ reach understandings on a Haredi draft-law framework
timeline.text: JFeed, citing a senior haredi source, reported late on November 26 that Yashar and United Torah Judaism had agreed on a draft-law framework: current enlistment targets would be dropped, oversight of yeshiva study tightened and extra enlistment tracks created. UTJ chair Yaakov Asher was reported to be due to put it to Rabbi Moshe Hillel Hirsch over the weekend, with lawyers for both sides to start drafting early next week if he agrees. The report is from a single outlet, and no coalition agreement with UTJ has been reported.

timeline.title: Likud officials expect Eisenkot to form a government without Likud
timeline.text: Citing Walla, senior Likud officials said the chances of a unity government were fading and Eisenkot was expected to form a government without Likud, possibly with haredi backing; Likud MK Amir Ohana called that the most likely outcome. Netanyahu met UTJ's Yaakov Asher and urged him not to rush. Reports also described a proposed three-month temporary measure to pause arrests of draft evaders pending a conscription law.

timeline.title: Democrats resume talks with Yashar; Education Ministry is the sticking point
timeline.text: Eisenkot said he had resolved the dispute with the Democrats and talks resumed on Thursday morning. The main open issue is the Education Ministry, which the Democrats want for MK Naama Lazimi and Yashar has so far kept. Reported preliminary allocations give Yisrael Beiteinu Defense, Justice and Aliyah and Integration, with Bennett tipped for Finance and Lapid for Foreign Affairs.

timeline.title: Liberman says UTJ has rabbis' approval and a government could be presented next week
timeline.text: In a Kan radio interview, Liberman said UTJ's lawmakers had received approval from their rabbis to negotiate and that talks were progressing well. He said he would accept a government backed by UTJ and possibly Ra'am, insisted it would have a Jewish majority rather than be a minority government, and expected it could be presented by the end of next week. Reports say UTJ's team would be led by Yaakov Asher.

timeline.title: First coalition pact: Yashar and Yisrael Beiteinu
timeline.text: After meeting Eisenkot, Liberman agreed to sign a coalition agreement with Yashar, the first since the election. The same day the Democrats were reported to have suspended talks with Eisenkot over his parallel talks with Likud.

timeline.title: Eisenkot plans a fast route to a confidence vote
timeline.text: Kan reported Eisenkot intends to announce he has a path to a government and bring it to a Knesset vote within days, leaving little time for pressure on partners. Liberman and UTJ's Ya'akov Asher opened a direct channel on haredi enlistment.

timeline.title: Second Likud–Yashar round ends without a deal
timeline.text: About four hours of talks covered a state commission of inquiry into October 7 and rolling back the judicial overhaul. Eisenkot's office said the core issue, a rotation agreement, was not discussed. A follow-up was announced with no date.

timeline.title: Eisenkot floats an 'emergency government'; Bennett backs unity under Eisenkot
timeline.text: Eisenkot said he would pursue an emergency government if broad talks fail. Bennett backed a unity government led by Eisenkot, exposing differences with Lapid over any role for Netanyahu.

timeline.title: Yashar's Matan Kahana elected Knesset speaker
timeline.text: Kahana beat Likud's Ofir Katz 66–52, an early show of strength for the anti-Netanyahu camp, though not a guide to how parties will vote on a government. Eisenkot said he would not drag out talks and would form a minority government if needed.

timeline.title: Likud and Yashar open formal talks; haredi track takes shape
timeline.text: Likud sent MK Ofir Katz and attorney Michael Rabello; Yashar sent MK Chili Tropper and Yoav Horowitz. Netanyahu called for a unity government. In parallel, Eisenkot's bloc was reported to be weighing a promise to freeze draft enforcement, including arrests of draft evaders, for up to a year to win haredi support. UTJ was reluctant to join without Shas.

timeline.title: 26th Knesset sworn in, with no new government
timeline.text: A Yashar-chaired Arrangements Committee was approved 63–50, giving Eisenkot's camp control of early Knesset business. Eisenkot said his bloc would not give up on drafting haredi men.

timeline.title: Reports of a secret Liberman–haredi channel
timeline.text: Israeli media reported that Liberman had spent months meeting the ultra-Orthodox parties about a possible draft compromise, shifting talk toward a haredi deal.

timeline.title: Eisenkot formally receives the mandate
timeline.text: Herzog handed Eisenkot 28 days to form a government, to December 6, extendable by 14 days. Eisenkot said he was open to Netanyahu joining.

timeline.title: Herzog picks Eisenkot
timeline.text: After meeting both Netanyahu and Eisenkot separately, the president announced he would task Eisenkot.

timeline.title: Consultations end: Eisenkot 67, Netanyahu 46
timeline.text: The Joint List backed Eisenkot from outside, taking him to 67. UTJ's 7 seats recommended no one. Herzog cautioned that recommendations do not show who can actually build a majority.

timeline.title: Final results certified; consultations begin
timeline.text: The Central Elections Committee approved the official results and presented them to Herzog. Ra'am recommended Eisenkot, bringing him to 56.

timeline.title: The Democrats back Eisenkot
timeline.text: Yair Golan's party said it would recommend Eisenkot for prime minister.

timeline.title: Herzog sets consultations; Bennett and Liberman endorse Eisenkot
timeline.text: The president said talks with party leaders would start Nov 4. Together and Yisrael Beiteinu said they would recommend Eisenkot.

timeline.title: Count complete: no majority for anyone
timeline.text: Netanyahu's bloc finished with 53 seats, Eisenkot's with 48, and Arab parties a record 19. Likud stayed the largest party with 27. Likud claims of a 'stolen' election were rejected by the Central Elections Committee.

timeline.title: Election day: deadlock on exit polls
timeline.text: Turnout neared 78%, the highest since 1999. Exit polls showed the two blocs roughly level and both far from 61. Eisenkot said voters had rejected Netanyahu and warned against a second election; Netanyahu called for a right-wing government.

timeline.title: Eisenkot bloc aims to submit coalition deals to the Knesset by December 1–2
timeline.text: Citing Maariv, the Jerusalem Post reported that Yashar aims to sign and submit all coalition agreements by Tuesday, December 1, or Wednesday at the latest, and Channel 12 said Eisenkot hopes to sign Together and the Democrats before Shabbat. Channel 13 reported the Democrats were told they would get none of the four senior portfolios. Reports say Housing and a Knesset committee chair are earmarked for UTJ, which said it is focused on the draft, education and religious status quo rather than portfolios.

timeline.title: Yashar and the Democrats agree to sign a coalition deal
timeline.text: Hours after talks resumed, Yashar and the Democrats said in a joint statement that they had reached understandings on signing a coalition agreement; the formal signing had not yet been reported. Israel Hayom reported the Democrats would get an expanded Public Security ministry, Labor and Welfare, Communications, and Culture and Sport, plus the Knesset Constitution Committee chair. Yashar did not immediately confirm the portfolio split.

timeline.title: Bennett denies Haaretz report of a back channel to Netanyahu's camp
timeline.text: Haaretz reported that an aide to Bennett holds a secret channel with a Netanyahu representative, who allegedly offered seven Likud list slots to Eisenkot-bloc members willing to defect. Bennett called the report false.

timeline.title: Democrats deal agreed in principle: four ministries, signing still pending
timeline.text: Reports say the Democrats would receive an expanded Public Security Ministry plus Labor and Welfare, Communications, and Culture and Sports, along with the Knesset Constitution Committee chair and a Judicial Selection Committee seat; the Justice and Education posts they sought were not included. Both reports describe the deal as agreed in principle with details still being finalized, not signed. National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir said he would fight such a government if it is formed.

timeline.title: Report: UTJ would not back a Democrats MK for Education; UTJ denies talks on posts
timeline.text: Citing a haredi outlet, Times of Israel reported that UTJ would not support Democrats MK Gilad Kariv as education minister and that Eisenkot agreed, with health and housing reportedly reserved for UTJ. UTJ denied negotiating cabinet posts with Eisenkot, and Yashar is said to be in informal talks with it on a draft framework. Shas has reportedly declined to join.
